text:
Toni: onboarding new HF model (llama-ish checkpoint) to Redwood Dedicated — streaming outputs stop early for some prompts, looks like EOS detected too soon.
Sam: can you paste a minimal repro and the config.json you used?
Toni: repro: short convo with assistant prompt. tokenizer shows eos token is '' in HF but tokenizer.encode yields two token ids on some inputs. snippet:
Toni: ```python
from transformers import AutoTokenizer
tok = AutoTokenizer.from_pretrained('hf-llama-test')
print(tok.eos_token, tok.eos_token_id)
print(tok.encode(''))
```
Anya: I ran that locally — eos_token is '', eos_token_id = 2, but for some chat templates the tokenizer splits that into [2, 125] when there is trailing spacing.
Mike: hmm, Redwood streaming stops when decoded text contains stop sequence string, not always when eos token id seen. If tokenizer produces multi-token sequence for the textual EOS or produces different byte sequences between HF and our tokenizer, that could trigger earlier-than-expected stop.
Toni: exact observed behavior: HF generate (non-streaming) returns full answer. Redwood streaming terminates ~30-40 tokens earlier on some seeds. Logs show "stop sequence matched" at client-side decoder.
Sam: any chance quantization changed token ids? which quant profile did you test?
Toni: tested float32 and int8 (bitsandbytes). int8 had same stop points for this model, so it's probably a decoding/detector mismatch rather than numeric instability.
Anya: found two issues in conversion checklist: special_tokens_map.json was missing `{'eos_token': ''}` mapping in the converted model package, and chat template used a literal `` in system prompt which got normalized away.
Mike: we should detect stop via token ids not decoded substrings during streaming. That avoids multibyte/normalization differences. Also handle multiple EOS tokens: some models define both `` and '<|endoftext|>' -> choose canonical single id and map aliases in tokenizer config.
Toni: quick mitigation I tested: added explicit `stop_token_ids = [tok.eos_token_id, tok.convert_tokens_to_ids('<|endoftext|>')]` and in streaming loop check last N token ids for any match before doing text-based stop. That fixed the early termination in most repros.
Sam: can you paste the minimal change we can apply in the HF-to-Redwood conversion script?
Toni: sure, small patch to conversion step:
Toni: ```diff
- config['eos_token'] = model.config.eos_token
+ # normalize eos to a single canonical token id and include aliases
+ eos = model.config.eos_token or ''
+ eos_id = tokenizer.convert_tokens_to_ids(eos)
+ aliases = []
+ for alt in ['<|endoftext|>', '</s>']:
+     aid = tokenizer.convert_tokens_to_ids(alt)
+     if aid is not None and aid != eos_id:
+         aliases.append(aid)
+ config['eos_token_id'] = str(eos_id)
+ config['eos_alias_ids'] = [str(x) for x in aliases]
```
Anya: note: `convert_tokens_to_ids` returns None for unknown tokens on some tokenizer implementations; guard for that. Also make sure we persist alias list to the runtime metadata so streaming decoder can consult token ids instead of raw string matches.
Mike: another edge: fast vs slow tokenizer differences. Fast tokenizer may merge special tokens differently. For streaming we must use same tokenization logic as the model served runtime. If the runtime tokenization differs from our client-side decoded substring matching, stops will be misaligned.
Toni: good point — we saw a case where HF `use_fast=True` produced different token boundaries than the Rust tokenizer in our runtime. I added a conversion test: tokenizing a canonical marker and ensuring the runtime and HF tokenizer IDs match exactly.
Sam: what about chat templates? could role markers like `<|assistant|>` be treated as stop?
Toni: yes: our default chat template appended `
Assistant: ` which together with model tokenizer produced an immediate eos token for some initial outputs. We changed templates to include explicit separators and avoid trailing whitespace right before expected assistant content.
Anya: TL;DR action items:
Anya: 1) Update conversion script to write eos_token_id and alias ids (as strings) into package metadata.
Anya: 2) Add unit that tokenizes canonical stop strings with both HF tokenizer and runtime tokenizer and fail conversion if mismatch.
Anya: 3) Change streaming detector to check token-id sequences (with alias support) before doing substring matches.
Anya: 4) Add test cases reproducing the early-stop prompts (both float32 and int8).
Mike: I've opened a follow-up ticket for runtime change + conversion tests. deploy-bot: deploy pipeline check triggered for branch `fix/eos-detection` and lint passed.
deploy-bot: https://ci.internal/redwood/pipeline/12345
Toni: thanks — I'll follow up with a short PR that adds the alias mapping and unit tests. Anyone want to review once I draft it?
Sam: I can review the conversion script changes.
Anya: I'll add the unit test harness to eng-ml test suite.
Mike: assigning to Sam/Toni/Anya to shepherd through QA. :thumbsup:
